WalkthroughText: An if-else statement lets your program choose between two paths based on a boolean condition. Java first evaluates the condition in the if's parentheses; if it's true, only the if block's statements run and the else block is skipped entirely. If the condition is false, the if block is skipped and only the else block runs. Because the program jumps between these blocks rather than running every line top to bottom, tracing execution means highlighting only the lines that actually run for a given condition.

PracticeItems.Explanation: Since temp (68) is not greater than 75, the condition is false, so the else branch runs, printing "Not hot". Only one branch of an if-else can ever execute, so the last choice is impossible.

PracticeItems.Prompt: Which statement about an if-else statement is true?
Choices: Both the if block and the else block always execute, in order.
Exactly one of the if block or the else block executes, depending on the boolean condition.
The else block only runs if the if condition throws an error.
The if block runs first no matter what, then the else block checks a second condition.
PracticeItems.Explanation: An if-else statement evaluates one boolean condition and executes exactly one of the two branches: the if block runs when the condition is true, and the else block runs when it is false. The other choices misdescribe control flow — both blocks never run together, and else doesn't depend on errors.

WalkthroughSteps.Caption: Here's our method: it checks whether a number is even or odd using an if-else statement. Let's trace it line by line starting at the top.
Line 2 is the if statement. Java evaluates the condition n % 2 == 0 to decide which branch to take.
n is 7, so n % 2 is 1, and 1 == 0 is false. The condition resolves to false.
Because the condition is false, the if block on line 3 is skipped completely — notice we do NOT highlight that line at all.
Line 4 is the else keyword. Since the if condition was false, control jumps here to run the else block instead.
Line 5, inside the else block, executes: it prints "Odd". This is the only branch that runs for this input.
After the else block finishes, execution continues after the whole if-else, skipping any remaining branches — the method returns.
